Festive Season Budget Strained as Onion and Pulse Prices Rise in Una

Rising Prices Impact Household Kitchens

As households prepare for festive celebrations, residents in Una are facing increased financial strain due to rising prices of essential kitchen commodities. Official data indicates that the costs of everyday items—including onions, lentils, and sugar—have seen noticeable upward adjustments over the past week, complicating household expense management during a peak festive period.

According to figures released by the local Statistics Department, onions have registered an increase of up to 8.33 percent, while chana dal and urad dal have climbed by 6.38 percent and 5.79 percent, respectively. Assistant Research Officer Mahendra Kumar noted that while many food items had previously remained steady, recent market rates reflect notable increases in specific staples.

Specific Commodity Price Changes

Market rates for several daily-use items have shifted over a single week:

  • Urad Dal (Whole): Rose from 121 rupees to 128 rupees per kilogram, an increase of 7 rupees.
  • Chana Dal: Increased from 94 rupees to 100 rupees per kilogram, a rise of 6 rupees.
  • Onions: Moved from 60 rupees to 65 rupees per kilogram, marking a 5-rupee hike.
  • Sugar (M-30): Climbed from 58 rupees to 61 rupees per kilogram, adding 3 rupees.
  • Parmal Rice: Slipped up by 1 rupee, moving from 38 rupees to 39 rupees per kilogram.

Meanwhile, several other essential items remained stable compared to the previous week. Wheat flour held steady at 40 rupees per kilogram, potatoes remained at 30 rupees per kilogram, and mustard oil stayed at 215 rupees per liter. Jaggery, vanaspati ghee, loose tea, and packed sugar also retained their previous price levels.

Practical Implications and Reader Verification

For residents managing household budgets during the festive season, these price shifts require closer tracking of grocery expenditures, particularly for vegetables and pulse varieties. Consumers can verify the official figures and ongoing market trends through local administrative price bulletins and the Una Statistics Department reports.
